title: Three-variable AM-GM over the constructed rationals, whose certificate FORCES a denominator-clearing scale
statement: For rationals a, b, c: (a*b + b*c) + c*a <= (a*a + b*b) + c*c. Equivalently ab + bc + ca <= a^2 + b^2 + c^2.

formal.statement: theorem Rat.mul_add_le_sq_add_sq_three : ((x0 : Rat) -> ((x1 : Rat) -> ((x2 : Rat) -> Rat.le (Rat.add (Rat.add (Rat.mul x0 x1) (Rat.mul x1 x2)) (Rat.mul x2 x0)) (Rat.add (Rat.add (Rat.mul x0 x0) (Rat.mul x1 x1)) (Rat.mul x2 x2)))))

evidence.supports: Rat.mul_add_le_sq_add_sq_three is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement, from a proof term the psatz PRODUCER searched for.
checkers: crate::psatz::rat::prove (the producer that emitted the term)
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example rat_theorem_inventory -- mul_add_le_sq_add_sq_three 2>/dev/null | grep -cE '^theorem[[:space:]]Rat\.mul_add_le_sq_add_sq_three[[:space:]]'
evidence.notes: The proof term was NOT written by a person. `crate::psatz::rat::prove` parsed the goal into a polynomial, factored the difference's Gram matrix over the affine basis with an exact rational LDL^T, cleared denominators to one integer scale, emitted the `sq_nonneg`/`add_nonneg` fold, proved the certificate's identity with `ring::rat::prove_eq`, and handed the assembled term to `Kernel::add_declaration`. `rat_prelude/psatz_inequalities.rs` has NO hand-written fallback: if the producer declines, `build_rat_prelude` fails, so the presence of this theorem in the environment is itself the evidence that the search ran and succeeded. `Kernel::add_declaration` re-checks the emitted term against the stated type, so a line in this tool's output for the exact name is a machine-checked proof having been admitted. `--release` is used for speed, not necessity: this binary builds logic/nat/int/rat and no constructed prelude. `grep -c` (never `-q`) both avoids a SIGPIPE-under-pipefail false negative and independently asserts the whitespace-anchored `theorem` row is present, so a theorem demoted to an axiom would fail this check rather than pass it. A named filter matching nothing exits 1 in the tool itself, verified 2026-09-05 (`no_such_rat_theorem_xyz` -> exit 1), so a deleted theorem cannot read as a re-derived one. The separators are `[[:space:]]`, not `\t`: POSIX ERE does not interpret `\t` as a tab, so a tab-anchored pattern matches NOTHING under the GNU grep a script gets, while an interactive shell's ugrep wrapper masks it.

The two counts that MOVED are the mutants that now also break `build_rat_prelude`, which is what the no-fallback design predicts. This row pins the PRODUCER's guards, not the statement: it says the search cannot silently degrade, and says nothing about the statement being true, which the kernel-term row above is what settles.

Canonical type copied verbatim from `target/release/examples/rat_theorem_inventory mul_add_le_sq_add_sq_three`, one name per invocation, release build. depends_on is the direct-edge set from `target/release/examples/theorem_dependency_inventory Rat.mul_add_le_sq_add_sq_three`, one name per invocation, restricted to edges that are themselves registered ledger facts -- every edge was, so nothing was dropped.

notes: Certificate: `4p = (2a - b - c)^2 + 3(b - c)^2`, i.e. one copy of the first square and three of the second, at scale 4. The scale is FORCED, not chosen: the Gram matrix of `a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-bc-ca` has half-integer off-diagonals and a quadratic form's Gram matrix is unique, so no unit-weight integer-form decomposition of it exists at all. The clearing is needed because `ring::rat`, which proves the certificate's identity, recognizes only the literals -1/0/1 -- a rational literal in this kernel is a normalized num/den pair with no free structural reduction, so a rational weight would be an opaque ATOM to the normalizer and the identity would not close. This is the ONLY one of the three whose dependency edges include `Rat.le_or_lt`, `Rat.le_of_lt`, `Rat.add_lt_add_of_le_of_lt`, `Rat.zero_add`, `Rat.lt_of_le_of_lt` and `Rat.lt_irrefl`: that is the producer's `divide_by_scale` step, which takes the scale back out by case-splitting on `le_or_lt` and folding a strict inequality to a contradiction, so the scale never reaches the statement. depends_on is the measured direct-edge set from `theorem_dependency_inventory`.
